cases.reason: In 2002 a continuation line of a literal may be a debugging line: the continuation line is 'the next line that is not a comment line or a blank line' (6.2.4), a debugging line is not a comment line until after COPY/REPLACE processing (6.2.7), and the program-text area of a D line may hold character-strings (6.2.3). SR6 therefore governs a continuation line carrying a fixed D indicator or a floating >>D indicator (6.1.2 table; for >>D the first nonblank character of the line is the indicator, not the quotation symbol), and how it interacts with logical conversion step 5 (a D line becomes a NEW >>D line, not an appended continuation). 2023 has no debugging indicator at all (6.2.3.1 table lists *>, >>, "-/'- only), so the 2023 row's witnesses (alphanumeric/national/boolean continuation on source lines) show nothing about this 2002 scope. Probes: at --std 2002 the compiler refuses a D-line continuation whose program-text area begins with the quote (r1a, COBOL2684 + COBOL3473 citing 2023) and refuses a >>D continuation line (r1c); it accepts a >>D line continued onto a plain line (r1d, prints ABCD). Whether r1a's refusal is right under 2002 turns on whether logical-conversion step 5 or step 9 governs a D continuation line: a 2002 witness and a signed reading are needed.

cases.reason: The rule defers to 'the rules of reference format', and those rules differ: 2002 permits continuing a COBOL word (and picture character-strings, numeric literals) with a fixed continuation indicator (6.2.4; logical conversion 6.4 step 7b), while 2023 removed continuation of COBOL words (Annex E.2 item 1; 2023 6.3.5 states continuation only for literals). So in 2002 a COBOL word inside COPY pseudo-text may be split across lines; at 2023 it is an error. Probe r2a: COPY CBR REPLACING ==TOK / -EN1== BY =="NEW"== prints NEW at --std 2002 and is refused at --std 2023 (COBOL0902 'continuation of a COBOL word ... removed in COBOL-2023'). The reader's witnesses (floating continuation of a literal, a fixed-continued literal) do not show the word case.

cases.reason: In 2002 pseudo-text-2 may contain debugging lines (SR10), and GR10 is the only REPLACE rule that places inserted pseudo-text-2 text-words ('placed in accordance with the rules of free-form reference format', which in 2002 include debugging lines, 6.3.4). GR11 covers only text being replaced that begins on a debugging line, so the reader's 'placement on debugging lines is GR11's' does not cover a debugging line inside pseudo-text-2 replacing text on a source line (COPY has GR13 for this; REPLACE leans on GR10). 2023 has no debugging lines, so the 2023 row's witness (l1c24) cannot show this part. Probe r4: REPLACE ==TOKEN1== BY =="A" / D DISPLAY "B" == prints A,END without DEBUGGING MODE and A,B,END with it at --std 2002 (the debugging line is kept); refused at 2023 (COBOL0902).

cases.reason: The state machine is word-identical, but the set of REPLACE statements 'encountered' is larger in 2002: a REPLACE may be written anywhere in source text (SR1), including on a debugging line, and 6.2.7 names REPLACE explicitly: a debugging line becomes comment-like only AFTER COPY and REPLACE processing, so a format 1 REPLACE on a D or >>D line is encountered and becomes active even without WITH DEBUGGING MODE. 2023 has no debugging lines, so a 2002 implementation that dropped debugging lines before text manipulation would pass every 2023 witness (pb1357) and violate this rule. Probe r3a: D-line REPLACE ==TOKEN1== BY =="NEW"== then DISPLAY TOKEN1 prints NEW at --std 2002 with and without DEBUGGING MODE; refused at 2023.
